title: Taller keycaps: Positive-ink invoice
summary: For every reading, produce the distance to the first strictly larger reading to its right, or 0 if none exists. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.
descriptionMd:
A repair clerk waits for a taller keycap before closing each unresolved height ticket. Sol prepares an invoice that accepts only positive ink adjustments. Zero and negative derived readings stay off the invoice.

For every reading, produce the distance to the first strictly larger reading to its right, or 0 if none exists.

Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist.

Implement tallerKeycapsPositiveInkInvoice(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Monotonic stacks. For every reading, produce the distance to the first strictly larger reading to its right, or 0 if none exists. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with monotonic stacks. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For every reading, produce the distance to the first strictly larger reading to its right, or 0 if none exists. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [4,1,2,1,0]. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 8.
The derived sequence is [0,0,1,0]. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 1.
The derived sequence is []. Return the sum of strictly positive values in the derived sequence, or 0 when none exist. This gives 0.
